title: Design a Load Balancer
summary: Design a Layer 7 load balancer for a web application.
body:
Design a Layer 7 load balancer for a web application.

## Scenario

Design a load balancer that distributes HTTP traffic across backend servers with health checking and session affinity.

## Requirements

- Multiple load balancing algorithms (round robin, least connections, weighted)
- Health checking with automatic server removal/addition
- Session affinity (sticky sessions) support
- SSL termination
- Request rate limiting per client IP

## Constraints

- Handle 100K concurrent connections
- Add/remove backend servers with zero downtime
- Failover in < 5 seconds
- No single point of failure for the load balancer itself

## What a strong answer covers

- L4 vs L7 load balancing tradeoffs
- Health check design (active vs passive)
- Consistent hashing for session affinity
- High availability of the load balancer itself
- Connection draining during server removal

## Reference walkthrough

L7 reverse proxy (like Nginx/HAProxy). Active health checks every 5s + passive monitoring of response errors. Consistent hashing on session cookie for affinity (falls back to round-robin for new sessions). SSL termination at LB with certificate management. HA via active-passive pair with VRRP/keepalived. Connection draining: stop sending new requests to removed server, wait for in-flight to complete (30s timeout). Rate limiting via token bucket per client IP in shared memory.
keyTakeaways: L4 vs L7 load balancing tradeoffs
High availability of the load balancer itself
